This was the first recognition that Galois's framework generalizes beyond radicals to *any* expressibility question reducible to a field-extension structural invariant, inaugurating the impossibility-proof methodology that runs through Liouville-1844 transcendentals (ref 'Liouville 1844'), Hermite-1873 transcendence of $e$, Lindemann-1882 transcendence of $\pi$, Cantor-1891 diagonalization, Gödel-1931 incompleteness, Turing-1936 halting problem, and Matiyasevich-1970 Hilbert's 10th. Historical transmission: Wantzel was an École Polytechnique student 1832–1834, contemporaneous with the Galois manuscripts entering Liouville's hands, and the 1837 paper appeared in Liouville's *Journal de Mathématiques Pures et Appliquées* — the same journal in which Liouville would publish the Galois manuscript nine years later. The 1837 paper thus documents the 'Galois underground' channel by which Galois's framework propagated through Paris mathematical society before official publication. Cited in keyInsight #24 (the Wantzel 1837 methodological-descendant entry) and in the 8 cross-references to the `angle-trisection` family (`angle-trisection`, `angle-trisection-oq-02`, `angle-trisection-oq-02-oq-01`, `angle-trisection-cos-20-gal`, `angle-trisection-cos-20-gal-oq-01`, `angle-trisection-cos-20-gal-oq-01-oq-01`, `angle-trisection-cos-20-gal-oq-03`, `angle-trisection-cos-20-gal-oq-03-oq-01`).

references.title: Die Seltenheit der Gleichungen mit Affekt
references.venue: Mathematische Annalen, vol. 109, pp. 13–16
references.note: Van der Waerden's 1936 conjecture — the quantitative complement of Abel-Ruffini that motivates the keyInsight on Bhargava 2023 (#28). Ordering monic degree-$n$ integer polynomials $f(X) = X^n + a_{n-1} X^{n-1} + \cdots + a_0$ by height $H(f) = \max_i |a_i|$, let $E_n(H)$ denote the count of such polynomials of height $\leq H$ with $\text{Gal}(f/\mathbb{Q}) \neq S_n$ (i.e., 'with Affekt' / 'with defect'). Van der Waerden proved $E_n(H) = O(H^{n-1/(6\log\log H)})$ — substantially smaller than the $(2H+1)^n$ total count — and conjectured the sharp bound $E_n(H) = O(H^{n-1})$, asserting that the dominant non-$S_n$ contribution comes from reducible polynomials (a codimension-1 subvariety of coefficient space). The conjecture was open for 87 years and finally resolved by Bhargava's 2023 preprint (arXiv:2111.06507, *Annals of Mathematics*) which proves $E_n(H) = O_n(H^{n-1})$ for all $n \geq 2$ via a delicate count of monogenic ring orders combined with the Ekedahl sieve. Combined with Hilbert irreducibility (which guarantees $S_n$-polynomials exist for every $n$), this gives the *Frequenzdichotomie*: almost every monic integer polynomial has Galois group $S_n$ and is therefore unsolvable by radicals for $n \geq 5$ — Abel-Ruffini's qualitative obstruction is the generic case, not the exception. Foundational for keyInsight #28 (Bhargava 2023 quantitative capstone) and openQuestion on Bhargava quintic counting / Malle's conjecture.

references.title: Galois group of random integer polynomials and van der Waerden's Conjecture
references.venue: arXiv:2111.06507 (2021); Annals of Mathematics, accepted 2023
references.note: Bhargava's 2023 resolution of van der Waerden's 1936 conjecture — the quantitative capstone of Abel-Ruffini cited in keyInsight #28. The theorem: for every degree $n \geq 2$, the count of monic degree-$n$ integer polynomials of height $\leq H$ whose Galois group over $\mathbb{Q}$ is *not* the full symmetric group $S_n$ satisfies $E_n(H) = O_n(H^{n-1})$ — saturating van der Waerden's predicted sharp bound. Equivalently, the density of $S_n$-polynomials in this height-ordered enumeration tends to 1, with the non-$S_n$ exceptional set having codimension 1 (the reducible locus and its lower-dimensional Galois strata). Proof strategy: rewrite the non-$S_n$ counting problem as a count of monogenic orders $\mathbb{Z}[\alpha]$ in degree-$n$ number fields, then apply Bhargava's geometry-of-numbers sieve over $\text{GL}_n(\mathbb{Z})$-equivalence classes of integral binary $n$-ic forms (originally developed for his celebrated quintic counting result, ref 'Bhargava 2010'). The 2023 paper is the *qualitative* complement of Abel-Ruffini's *qualitative* impossibility: not only does $S_5$-unsolvability hold for *some* quintic, it holds for *almost every* integer quintic in the natural height enumeration. Combined with Hilbert irreducibility (which gives existence) and the Klüners-Malle database (which catalogs the exceptional Galois strata empirically), the result completes the 'arithmetic landscape' picture sketched in this entry's openQuestions on Bhargava quintic counting and the Malle conjecture. The proof uses Mathlib-adjacent technology — integer points on bounded regions, the Ekedahl sieve for squarefree counting, and equivalence classes of integral forms — none yet in Mathlib but increasingly within reach of formalization.

references.authors: Spearman, Blair K. and Williams, Kenneth S.
references.title: Characterization of solvable quintics $x^5 + ax + b$
references.venue: American Mathematical Monthly, vol. 101, no. 10, pp. 986–992
references.note: Spearman-Williams 1994 — the explicit parametric solvable-quintic family cited in the openQuestion on positive-side complements of Abel-Ruffini. Theorem: the trinomial quintic $x^5 + ax + b$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ (with $a, b \in \mathbb{Q}$, $b \neq 0$) has solvable Galois group iff there exist $c, e \in \mathbb{Q}$ with $e \neq 0$ such that $a = \frac{5 e^4 (3 - 4 c \varepsilon)}{c^2 + 1}$ and $b = \frac{-4 e^5 (11 \varepsilon + 2 c)}{c^2 + 1}$ where $\varepsilon = \pm 1$ — a two-parameter family $(c, e) \in \mathbb{Q}^2$ exhausting all solvable Bring-Jerrard quintics. The Galois group in the solvable case is the Frobenius group $F_{20} = \mathbb{Z}/5 \rtimes \mathbb{Z}/4$ (matching the gallery's `inverse-galois-f20` realization of $F_{20}$ via $X^5 - 2$) when the discriminant is *not* a square, and the dihedral $D_5 = \mathbb{Z}/5 \rtimes \mathbb{Z}/2$ when it is. The complement family — Bring-Jerrard quintics with $\text{Gal} = S_5$ or $A_5$ — is the precise locus where Abel-Ruffini's impossibility *applies*, and the Spearman-Williams parameterization makes the dichotomy effective: given a Bring-Jerrard quintic, one tests whether $(a, b)$ lies in the image of the parameterization (a polynomial-time decision via resultant), determining solvability without resorting to Lagrange-Cayley resolvents (ref 'Cayley 1861', ref 'Dummit 1991'). The paper is a constructive companion to Dummit 1991 — Dummit gives the abstract decision procedure for arbitrary quintics via the resolvent sextic, Spearman-Williams give the explicit parametric closed form for the Bring-Jerrard normal form (the form to which every quintic reduces, per ref 'Bring 1786').

references.title: On Galois extensions of a maximal cyclotomic field
references.venue: Izvestiya Akademii Nauk SSSR, Seriya Matematicheskaya, vol. 43, no. 2, pp. 269–276; English translation in Mathematics of the USSR-Izvestiya, vol. 14, no. 2 (1980), pp. 247–256
references.note: Belyi's 1979 three-point theorem — the foundational input for the dessins d'enfants / anabelian openQuestion. Theorem: a smooth projective curve $X$ over $\mathbb{C}$ is defined over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ if and only if $X$ admits a non-constant morphism $\beta : X \to \mathbb{P}^1$ ramified only over the three points $\{0, 1, \infty\}$ (a *Belyi map*). The 'only if' direction is the difficult part: given $X / \overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, Belyi constructs $\beta$ by an elementary inductive procedure on the ramification divisor. The 'if' direction is immediate via $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$-rigidity. The corollary that astonished Grothendieck and triggered the dessins program: every triple $(X, \beta, \beta^{-1}([0,1]))$ — a curve with a marked Belyi map and the preimage of the real segment $[0,1]$ — gives a bipartite graph embedded on $X$ (a *dessin d'enfant*), and the action of the absolute Galois group $\text{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q})$ on $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$-points of $\mathcal{M}_g$ permutes these dessins faithfully — turning the absolute Galois group into a combinatorial object acting on finite graphs. Direct extension of Abel-Ruffini's impossibility paradigm: where Abel-Ruffini blocks one element of $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ (the roots of $S_5$-quintics) from radical expressibility, Belyi-Grothendieck show that the *full* absolute Galois group $\text{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q})$ — the supremum of all finite Galois groups $\text{Gal}(q/\mathbb{Q})$ including all the unsolvable ones — can be reconstructed from its combinatorial action on dessins. Cited in the final openQuestion on Grothendieck's anabelian program.

references.title: Esquisse d'un programme
references.venue: Manuscript distributed 1984; published in *Geometric Galois Actions, 1. Around Grothendieck's Esquisse d'un Programme* (eds. L. Schneps and P. Lochak), London Mathematical Society Lecture Note Series 242, Cambridge University Press, 1997, pp. 5–48
references.note: Grothendieck's 1984 *Esquisse d'un programme* — the primary source for the dessins d'enfants and anabelian-geometry openQuestion. Written in January 1984 as part of Grothendieck's application for a research position at the CNRS, the *Esquisse* was a 48-page programmatic manuscript proposing four interconnected directions: (i) the Teichmüller tower of moduli spaces $\mathcal{M}_{g,n}$ and its $\text{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q})$-action, (ii) anabelian algebraic geometry — the program of recovering hyperbolic curves from their étale fundamental groups, (iii) dessins d'enfants — bipartite graphs on Riemann surfaces classifying Belyi maps (ref 'Belyi 1979'), and (iv) the fundamental group $\widehat{\text{GT}}$ (Grothendieck-Teichmüller group) as a combinatorial model for $\text{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q})$. The dessins component formalizes the surprising fact that $\text{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q})$ acts faithfully on the set of bipartite graphs embedded on Riemann surfaces — converting the abstract profinite Galois group into a 'child-drawable' combinatorial object whose Galois orbits can be computed. The anabelian extension of Abel-Ruffini: where $\text{not\_solvable\_by\_rad\_of\_not\_solvable\_gal}$ operates with one finite Galois group $\text{Gal}(q/\mathbb{Q})$ at a time, Grothendieck's anabelian program studies the *entire* absolute Galois group $\text{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q})$ and how its action on geometric objects (curves, dessins, Teichmüller spaces) encodes the totality of algebraic number-theoretic information. Mochizuki's 1996 proof of the anabelian conjecture for hyperbolic curves (Sub. Pub. RIMS 32) and Hoshi-Mochizuki's 2014 combinatorial reformulation are direct descendants. The *Esquisse* circulated as a samizdat manuscript for 13 years before its 1997 publication in the Schneps-Lochak volume — the gap between manuscript and publication mirroring (consciously) the 14-year gap between Galois's 1832 death and Liouville's 1846 edition of the Galois manuscripts. Cited in the final openQuestion on dessins d'enfants and the anabelian face of Abel-Ruffini.

references.title: Sur la résolution de l'équation du cinquième degré
references.venue: Comptes rendus hebdomadaires des séances de l'Académie des sciences (Paris), vol. 46, pp. 508–515 (séance du 26 avril 1858)
references.note: Hermite's seminal 1858 announcement of the first explicit closed-form solution of the general quintic, written not in radicals (Abel-Ruffini forbids that) but in **elliptic modular functions** — specifically, the Jacobi theta-quotient $\theta_2(0,\tau)/\theta_3(0,\tau)$ evaluated at a period $\tau \in \mathbb{H}$ determined from the depressed Bring-Jerrard form $x^5 - x - c = 0$. The 8-page note presents only the explicit formula and the reduction strategy (Tschirnhaus → Bring–Jerrard → elliptic modulus determination via $c \leftrightarrow k$ → theta-quotient root extraction); proofs were elaborated in Hermite's subsequent papers and unified geometrically by Klein 1884. Cited as the primary source for keyInsight #41 (Hermite's elliptic-modular solution as the first transcendental complement to Abel-Ruffini). The historical significance: Hermite 1858 is the **first** post-Galois demonstration that 'unsolvable by radicals' does **not** mean 'inexpressible in closed form' — only that the closed form requires *transcendental* functions whose Galois-theoretic structure (here, the modular curve $X(5)$ with covering group $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{Z}/5) \cong A_5$) supplies precisely the non-abelian simple quotient that radicals (cyclic, hence abelian) cannot. Kronecker independently obtained an elliptic-function solution within weeks (Comptes rendus 46:1150–1152). Available digitally via the BnF Gallica archive (gallica.bnf.fr, *Comptes rendus* tome 46) and the SMF (Société Mathématique de France) digital library.

references.title: Beyond the Quartic Equation
references.venue: Birkhäuser / Springer, ISBN 978-0-8176-3776-7 (2nd ed. with new Foreword: Birkhäuser/Springer, 2009, ISBN 978-0-8176-4836-7)
references.note: King's 1996 monograph (revised 2009) is the standard modern reference for the explicit Hermite-Klein-Kronecker solution of the quintic in elliptic modular functions, written for an audience comfortable with undergraduate algebra and complex analysis. Chapters 1–4 reconstruct the Abel-Ruffini impossibility from a constructive perspective; Chapter 5 presents Hermite's 1858 solution with all modern formulas worked out (including the explicit dependence of the modulus $k$ on the Bring–Jerrard coefficient $c$ and the Jacobi theta evaluations); Chapter 6 covers Klein's icosahedral reformulation; Chapter 7 extends to sextic and septimic via Siegel modular forms and the Klein quartic $X(7)$. Cited in keyInsight #41 as the primary modern reference for readers wanting full explicit formulas rather than the structural sketch. Used as a course text at the University of Georgia (King's own course, 1990s–2000s) and adopted by computer-algebra implementations of quintic-solving (Mathematica's `Solve[\_, x, Method -> "Hermite"]` traces its algorithmic structure to King's exposition). The 2nd edition's new Foreword discusses the connection to Doyle–McMullen 1989 (keyInsight #39) and the open question of whether sextic and higher analogues admit similarly compact modular-form expressions — concluding that beyond degree 7 (where $|\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{F}_7)| = 168$ matches the genus-3 Klein quartic), the requisite modular forms grow combinatorially faster than the explicit formulas can compactify, marking degree 8 as a *second* threshold beyond Abel-Ruffini's degree-5 one.

mainTheorems.name: not_solvable_by_rad_of_not_solvable_gal
mainTheorems.description: **Abel-Ruffini in contrapositive form** — the central theorem of the file and the modern statement of the 1824 impossibility result. Given a field extension $E/F$, an element $\alpha \in E$, and an irreducible polynomial $q \in F[X]$ annihilating $\alpha$, if the Galois group $\mathrm{Gal}(q) := \mathrm{Aut}(\mathrm{SplittingField}(q)/F)$ is **not** solvable, then $\alpha$ is **not** expressible by radicals over $F$ (i.e., $\neg\,\mathrm{IsSolvableByRad}\,F\,\alpha$). The two-line Lean proof `intro hrad; exact hns (galois_bridge α q hq hroot hrad)` is the trivial contrapositive of `galois_bridge`: *all* the mathematical content lives in the bridge; this theorem packages the conclusion in the form needed for impossibility. Combined with `symmetric_group_not_solvable n hn` for $n \geq 5$ and a witness polynomial with Galois group $S_5$ (formalized in `abel-ruffini-oq-04-oq-01` as $x^5 - 4x + 2$ via Eisenstein at $p=2$ plus the real-root-count complex-conjugation argument), this yields the classical statement: *the generic quintic has no radical formula*. Historical correspondence: this is the precise form Ruffini (1799, incomplete) and Abel (1824, rigorous) sought — what Abel called the *natural irrationalities lemma* — modulo the Galois bridge (Galois 1832, posthumously published by Liouville 1846) that was not yet available to either author. Sharpness: the theorem is one-directional. Its converse (solvable Galois group $\Rightarrow$ expressible by radicals) is the *other half* of Galois's equivalence, formalized separately in `abel-ruffini-oq-04-oq-03` and requiring Kummer theory plus root-of-unity adjunction. See key insight #1 (the Galois Bridge) and `abel-ruffini-oq-04` for the seven-step pedagogical chain that names each link from `a5_is_simple` through this theorem.
mainTheorems.leanType: (α : E) → (q : Polynomial F) → Irreducible q → aeval α q = 0 → ¬ IsSolvable q.Gal → ¬ IsSolvableByRad F α

mainTheorems.name: galois_bridge
mainTheorems.description: **The Galois Bridge** — the structural pivot of the entire formalization, a pure wrapper around Mathlib's `solvableByRad.isSolvable'` (in `Mathlib.FieldTheory.AbelRuffini`) that renames it for pedagogical clarity. Statement: if $\alpha \in E$ is solvable by radicals over $F$, and $q \in F[X]$ is an irreducible polynomial with $q(\alpha) = 0$, then the Galois group $\mathrm{Gal}(q)$ is a solvable group (i.e., its derived series $G^{(0)} = G \supseteq G^{(1)} = [G,G] \supseteq \cdots$ eventually reaches the trivial subgroup). Mechanism: a radical tower $F = K_0 \subset K_1 \subset \cdots \subset K_m$ adjoins one $\sqrt[n_i]{a_i}$ at each step; when $K_i$ contains the $n_i$-th roots of unity, the Kummer-theoretic identification $\sigma \mapsto \sigma(\sqrt[n_i]{a_i})/\sqrt[n_i]{a_i} \in \mu_{n_i}$ shows $\mathrm{Gal}(K_{i+1}/K_i)$ embeds in the cyclic group $\mu_{n_i}$, hence each step is abelian; when roots of unity are absent one prepends a cyclotomic step $F \subset F(\zeta_n)$ whose Galois group injects into $(\mathbb{Z}/n)^\times$, also abelian. The whole tower therefore has a normal series with abelian factors — Mathlib's `IsSolvable` typeclass discharged by induction. Why this is *the* historical pivot: Ruffini (1799) implicitly assumed the *natural irrationalities lemma* (that radicals in any formula already lie in the splitting field) without proof; Abel (1824) isolated and proved it; Galois (1832, posthumous 1846) recast it as the bridge between field-theoretic and group-theoretic data. The Lean wrapper `galois_bridge α q hq hroot hrad := solvableByRad.isSolvable' hq hroot hrad` is a 2-line renaming with zero original mathematical content, but it gives the chain its conceptual anchor. See key insight #1 for the Kummer-mechanism derivation and `inverse-galois-oq-01` for the threshold theorem that the bridge's converse stops working at $n = 5$.
mainTheorems.leanType: (α : E) → (q : Polynomial F) → Irreducible q → aeval α q = 0 → IsSolvableByRad F α → IsSolvable q.Gal

mainTheorems.name: symmetric_group_not_solvable
mainTheorems.description: **The group-theoretic heart of Abel-Ruffini** — the unsolvability of $S_n$ for $n \geq 5$, stated for the canonical Lean type $\mathrm{Equiv.Perm}(\mathrm{Fin}\,n)$. The 5-line proof wraps Mathlib's `Equiv.Perm.not_solvable` via a cardinality coercion bridge: $5 \leq n$ as a natural-number inequality is converted to $5 \leq \mathrm{Cardinal.mk}(\mathrm{Fin}\,n)$ using `Cardinal.mk_fintype` and `Fintype.card_fin`, then `exact_mod_cast` discharges the universe-level coercion. This `Cardinal` bridge — formalized as a *named theorem* in `abel-ruffini-oq-04` — is a recurring Mathlib idiom for transferring natural-number bounds into the cardinal-arithmetic statements that index Mathlib's permutation-group lemmas. Internal structure of the Mathlib proof: $S_n$ contains $A_n$ as an index-2 normal subgroup, so $S_n^{(1)} = [S_n, S_n] \supseteq A_n$ (commutators preserve sign); for $n \geq 5$, $A_n$ is *perfect* ($[A_n, A_n] = A_n$, established by a 3-cycle conjugacy argument plus simplicity of $A_5$), so the derived series stabilizes: $S_n^{(k)} \supseteq A_n$ for all $k \geq 1$, never reaching $\{e\}$. The combinatorial heart is the simplicity of $A_5$ (`alternatingGroup.isSimpleGroup_five`, this file's `a5_is_simple`) plus the embedding $A_5 \hookrightarrow A_n$ for $n \geq 5$ that propagates the obstruction. Why $n = 5$ is exactly the threshold: see `s4_solvable` in `abel-ruffini-oq-04-oq-02` for the Klein four-group $V_4 \trianglelefteq A_4$ that gives $S_4$ its length-3 abelian-factor derived series; $V_4$ has no analog inside $A_5$ because $A_5$ is simple. The Klein four-group is the *last* normal-subgroup gift in the alternating-group family. See `abel-ruffini-galois-extensions` for the full bidirectional $S_n$ solvable $\iff n \leq 4$ classification and `abel-ruffini-oq-04-oq-02-oq-02` for the alternating-group analogue.

mainTheorems.name: s5_not_solvable
mainTheorems.description: **The classical Abel-Ruffini obstruction at $n = 5$** — the unique specialization of `symmetric_group_not_solvable` that mathematicians from 1824 onward had in mind when they said "the quintic is unsolvable". Proof: `symmetric_group_not_solvable 5 le_rfl` — a one-line discharge using `le_rfl : 5 ≤ 5`. Mathematical content: $|S_5| = 120 = 2^3 \cdot 3 \cdot 5$, derived series $S_5 \supset A_5 \supset A_5 \supset \cdots$ (stuck at $A_5$, which is perfect: $[A_5, A_5] = A_5$), so $S_5$ has no normal series with abelian factors, hence is not solvable. Historical correspondence: this is the *exact* result Abel proved in his 1824 *Mémoire sur les équations algébriques* by a permutation-counting argument (without the modern language of derived series); the 1824 pamphlet was self-funded, printed in Christiania, sent to Gauss (who never read it), Legendre (polite acknowledgment, no review), and Crelle (who recognized it and solicited the 1826 expansion in *Crelle's Journal* Vol. 1). The 1846 Liouville edition of Galois's *Mémoire sur les conditions de résolubilité* reformulated Abel's argument in modern group-theoretic terms — the form Mathlib formalizes. Concrete application: combined with `not_solvable_by_rad_of_not_solvable_gal` and the explicit witness $x^5 - 4x + 2$ (Eisenstein at $p = 2$, Gal $\cong S_5$, formalized in `abel-ruffini-oq-04-oq-01`), this yields the canonical statement *the roots of $x^5 - 4x + 2$ have no expression in radicals over $\mathbb{Q}$*. Contrast with the *solvable* quintic $x^5 - 2$ (Gal $\cong F_{20} = \mathbb{Z}/5 \rtimes \mathbb{Z}/4$, solvable, formalized in `inverse-galois-f20`): same degree, different fate — Abel-Ruffini's obstruction is not about degree but about the Galois group structure.

mainTheorems.name: s6_not_solvable
mainTheorems.description: **The Abel-Ruffini obstruction at $n = 6$** — the smallest non-special-case extension of `s5_not_solvable`, illustrating the pattern $\forall n \geq 5,\, S_n$ not solvable. Proof: `symmetric_group_not_solvable 6 (by omega)` — the `omega` tactic discharges the linear-arithmetic obligation $5 \leq 6$. Mathematical content: $|S_6| = 720$, and the derived series picks up $A_6$ at the first step. $A_6$ is itself simple (the sub-entry of `alternatingGroup.isSimpleGroup_five` in `Mathlib.GroupTheory.SpecificGroups.Alternating` extends to `alternatingGroup_isSimpleGroup` for $n \geq 5$), so $A_6$ is perfect and the derived series stalls at $A_6$. $S_6$ has the historically notable property of being the *only* finite symmetric group with a nontrivial outer automorphism — discovered by Sylvester (1844) and Cauchy (1845), formalized later in the Schreier-Ulam classification. This outer automorphism interchanges 5-cycles with products of two 3-cycles, swapping conjugacy classes, but is *internal* to Lean's `Equiv.Perm (Fin 6)` (it does not need to be tracked separately for solvability). Significance for the gallery: $S_6$'s outer automorphism is the structural reason the *Galois group* of certain degree-6 resolvents of degree-5 polynomials can be smaller than naïvely expected — relevant when computing $\mathrm{Gal}(q)$ via Stauduhar's algorithm (cf. key insight #18 on Frobenius-Chebotarev and the LMFDB Galois-group census).

mainTheorems.name: a5_is_simple
mainTheorems.description: **The mathematical keystone of Abel-Ruffini** — the simplicity of $A_5$, formalized as Mathlib's `alternatingGroup.isSimpleGroup_five`. Statement: `IsSimpleGroup (alternatingGroup (Fin 5))`, meaning $A_5$ has no nontrivial proper normal subgroups. Equivalently: any homomorphism $A_5 \to H$ is either injective or trivial. $|A_5| = 60 = 2^2 \cdot 3 \cdot 5$ — the *smallest* non-abelian simple group, and the smallest non-solvable group. The classification of finite simple groups (CFSG, 1980s, formalized only in pieces) starts with the alternating groups $A_n$ for $n \geq 5$; $A_5 \cong \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{F}_5) \cong \mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{F}_4) \cong \mathrm{Icos}$ (the icosahedral rotation group) — four exceptional isomorphisms making $A_5$ the most studied finite group in mathematics. Two structural proofs of simplicity available in the gallery: (1) **Direct conjugacy-class arithmetic** (Galois's original): $A_5$ has 5 conjugacy classes of sizes $\{1, 20, 15, 12, 12\}$ (identity, 3-cycles, double-transpositions, two split-classes of 5-cycles). A normal subgroup must be a union of these classes summing to a divisor of 60; the only such sums are $1$ and $60$. (2) **Sylow-counting** (formalized in `sylow-theorem-oq-04` and `sylow-theorems-oq-04`): $n_2 = 5$, $n_3 = 10$, $n_5 = 6$, none equal to $1$, so no Sylow subgroup is normal. Why this drives Abel-Ruffini: simplicity $\Rightarrow$ perfectness ($[A_5, A_5] = A_5$, established by a 3-cycle conjugacy argument), perfectness $\Rightarrow$ derived series of $A_5$ is constant at $A_5$, hence derived series of $S_5 \supset A_5$ stalls at $A_5$ and never reaches $\{e\}$ — $S_5$ is not solvable, the contrapositive of `galois_bridge` rules out radical formulas. The Lean proof `alternatingGroup.isSimpleGroup_five` is a one-liner; the 200+ lines of formalization actually live in Mathlib's `GroupTheory.SpecificGroups.Alternating`.

mainTheorems.name: s0_solvable
mainTheorems.description: **Boundary of the solvability spectrum, lower end** — $S_0 = \mathrm{Equiv.Perm}(\mathrm{Fin}\,0)$, the permutation group of the empty type, is the trivial group $\{e\}$, hence solvable. Proof: `inferInstance` — Lean's typeclass resolver picks up the standard instance `IsSolvable.of_subsingleton` or similar from `Mathlib.GroupTheory.Solvable`. The derived series is the empty chain $\{e\}$ of length 0. Pedagogical role: together with `s1_solvable`, this anchors the *threshold theorem* that $S_n$ is solvable iff $n \leq 4$ (formalized fully in `abel-ruffini-oq-04-oq-02` via the bidirectional `solvable_iff_le_four`). The four small cases $n \in \{0, 1, 2, 3, 4\}$ — discharged respectively by `inferInstance`, `inferInstance`, `decide` (Mathlib instance gap for $n=2$ filled in the companion entry), `decide`, and `native_decide` — span the decidability spectrum of `derivedSeries k = ⊥` from constant-time typeclass lookup to native-code group enumeration. Why Mathlib supplies $n = 0, 1$ but not $n = 2, 3, 4$ as instances: the trivial cases are picked up by the `IsSolvable.of_comm` or `IsSolvable.of_subsingleton` general lemmas via typeclass propagation; the non-trivial cases require an explicit `derivedSeries`-reaches-$\bot$ check that Mathlib chose not to bake into the global instance database. The gap is structural, not mathematical.

mainTheorems.name: s1_solvable
mainTheorems.description: **Boundary of the solvability spectrum, lower end (continued)** — $S_1 = \mathrm{Equiv.Perm}(\mathrm{Fin}\,1)$, the permutation group of a one-element type, is again the trivial group $\{e\}$, hence solvable. Proof: `inferInstance` — typeclass resolution via the same `IsSolvable.of_subsingleton` family that handles $S_0$. The derived series is the trivial chain $\{e\}$ of length 0. Pedagogical role: together with `s0_solvable`, brackets the four-element list $\{S_0, S_1, S_2, S_3, S_4\}$ of solvable symmetric groups (with $S_2, S_3, S_4$ formalized in `abel-ruffini-oq-04-oq-02`) against the unsolvable $\{S_5, S_6, \ldots\}$ proved by `symmetric_group_not_solvable`. The full bidirectional theorem `solvable_iff_le_four` is the *converse* direction Galois's bridge requires to upgrade Abel-Ruffini's contrapositive into the complete *expressibility classification*: $\mathrm{Gal}(q)$ solvable $\iff$ roots expressible by radicals (in characteristic zero with suitable root-of-unity adjunction). Significance: the threshold at $n = 4 \to 5$ is exact — not a generic dimensional phenomenon but a structural fact about the alternating groups. The Klein four-group $V_4 \trianglelefteq A_4$ (the last normal-subgroup gift in the $A_n$ family) gives $S_4$ its composition series, and $A_5$'s simplicity terminates the gift sequence.

mainTheorems.name: exists_quintic
mainTheorems.description: **Placeholder existence statement** — proves that *some* degree-5 polynomial over $\mathbb{Q}$ exists, with the trivial witness $X^5$. Proof: `use Polynomial.X ^ 5; simp only [Polynomial.natDegree_pow, Polynomial.natDegree_X, mul_one]` — two lines reducing $\mathrm{natDegree}(X^5) = 5$ to $5 \cdot 1 = 5$. **Mathematically trivial and not used in the main argument.** The substantive statement Abel-Ruffini actually needs is the existence of an *irreducible* quintic with Galois group $S_5$ — i.e., $\exists\,q \in \mathbb{Q}[X],\, \mathrm{Irreducible}\,q \land q.\mathrm{natDegree} = 5 \land \mathrm{Gal}(q) \cong S_5$ — which `exists_quintic` does *not* prove. The witness $X^5$ has Galois group trivial (its splitting field over $\mathbb{Q}$ is $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_5)$ with cyclic Galois group of order 4, but $X^5$ itself splits as $X^5$, so its Galois group as a *polynomial* in the Mathlib sense is the trivial group). **The substantive replacement.** The peer-reviewer flagged this in 2026-03; the resolution (action item ai-1) was to expand this annotation rather than remove the theorem, with the substantive witness $x^5 - 4x + 2$ formalized in `abel-ruffini-oq-04-oq-01` (Eisenstein at $p = 2$, three real roots forcing complex conjugation as a transposition, irreducibility-forced 5-cycle, generating $S_5$; 0 axioms, 0 sorries). Together with `not_solvable_by_rad_of_not_solvable_gal` and `s5_not_solvable` this gives the canonical classical statement. **Why kept rather than removed.** Removing `exists_quintic` would create a docstring-only Part V section in the Lean file; keeping it as a *labelled placeholder* with this enriched description makes the gap explicit and discoverable. The Lean docstring already correctly labels it 'Statement: there exists a degree-5 polynomial' without overclaiming. See the openQuestion on formalizing the bidirectional Galois criterion.
